bug_semantics: In installations using elFinderVolumeMySQL, an authenticated requester can forge the target hash so the shared decoder yields SQL syntax instead of a numeric object id; cacheDir(), _joinPath(), _stat(), and _fopen() then interpolate that value into id or parent_id predicates, enabling SQL-query manipulation, data disclosure, and denial of service.
flaw_origin: Commit 357fc6f645056198c079d1d08d03cb46cdbaaacf changed the MySQL driver's path model from escaped filesystem paths to numeric database ids but retained the generic reversible hash decoder and made _abspath() an identity operation, then placed those unvalidated decoded ids directly into SQL. Later rewrites preserved and expanded the same omission; they are not the first causal writer.
ai_marker: absent: the BIC commit object names Dmitry Levashov <dio@std42.ru> as both author and committer and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer.
evidence: GitHub vendor advisory GHSA-c3gj-q88f-7hqj states that crafted target hashes are decoded without numeric-ID validation and reach cacheDir(), _joinPath(), _stat(), and _fopen(); affected versions are <=2.1.67 and patched version is 2.1.68: https://github.com/Studio-42/elFinder/security/advisories/GHSA-c3gj-q88f-7hqj

The official CVEProject cvelistV5 record for CVE-2026-44521 is PUBLISHED, describes authenticated SQL injection through a crafted target hash, marks versions <2.1.68 affected, and says 2.1.68 fixes it: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CVEProject/cvelistV5/main/cves/2026/44xxx/CVE-2026-44521.json

git show 357fc6f645056198c079d1d08d03cb46cdbaaacf shows the 'mysql driver now use id as path' change: generic decode() base64-decodes attacker-controlled hashes, MySQL _abspath() returns the decoded value unchanged, and new queries interpolate raw $path/$id into WHERE f.id, WHERE f.parent_id, and WHERE id predicates.

git show 03297033d07606e7eb09aab6409afdeebdbc6554:src/connectors/php/elFinderVolumeMySQL.class.php verifies the immediate parent lacks the numeric-id-as-path mechanism: fileinfo(), _scandir(), and _fopen() query filesystem path values after db->real_escape_string(); the 357fc6f parent diff therefore directly establishes absence.

git blame 2.1.67 php/elFinderVolumeMySQL.class.php attributes the surviving cacheDir/_joinPath/_stat/_fopen form to later 2019-2020 rewrites, while full-history path tracing reaches the earlier 357fc6f first introduction of the same unvalidated decoded-id invariant; the later changes are refactors, not the BIC.

git merge-base --is-ancestor 357fc6f645056198c079d1d08d03cb46cdbaaacf 2.1.67-src succeeds, and git diff --quiet confirms php/elFinderVolumeMySQL.class.php is byte-identical in tags 2.1.67-src and 2.1.67, placing the flaw in the affected release artifact.

Direct fix 6f7593fcac442644ecb00a999871aae966363bc1 adds normalizePathId()/pathId(), overrides decode() to reject non-digits, and applies numeric validation/formatting to cacheDir(), _joinPath(), _stat(), _fopen(), and the remaining MySQL id sinks; its parent 340e600d2abcf686f98bfc3499c8b6259fdc2d53 still has the raw interpolations.

git merge-base --is-ancestor 6f7593fcac442644ecb00a999871aae966363bc1 2.1.68-src succeeds; packaged build commit d03a9c7ad84ce0b6c33f25c2eb570e7d13d07fe9 carries the fix into tag 2.1.68, where normalizePathId is present, while tag 2.1.67 lacks it.
reasoning: The public history provides a complete lifecycle. The generic hash decoder accepts attacker-chosen base64 content; 357fc6f made that decoded content the MySQL object-id path and first sent it unvalidated into SQL. Its immediate parent used escaped filesystem paths, so the causal mechanism is absent there. Later rewrites changed function structure and line ownership but preserved the already-existing trust-boundary error. The 2026 direct fix validates decoded paths as digits and converts all SQL-facing ids to integers, and the corrected source is packaged in 2.1.68. Because the atomic BIC is a human-authored 2011 commit whose commit object has no AI marker, the real vulnerability is NOT_AI.
